comments.body: rebar-implement plan-review claim gate BLOCKED this story with 7 critical findings that collapse into two design flaws. (A) Merge mechanism [findings 1,2,5]: the heal's 'merge=union driver' is EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN in this codebase — init.py _GITATTRIBUTES documents 'merge=union is WRONG here — it line-unions JSON into invalid JSON'. (B) S3 object operations [findings 3,4,6,7 — NO suggested fix, premise-level]: the plan routes the DOCTOR lock marker (conditional-put/TTL/steal), bundle enumeration, and per-head bundle deletion 'through the helper's own S3 remote' with 'no direct S3 SDK use' (AC line 6), but git-remote-s3 is a git remote-helper SUBPROCESS speaking only the git protocol (ref list/fetch/push) — it exposes NO API for arbitrary S3 object ops or a conditional-put lock/TTL, and rebar's only helper touchpoint is require_s3_helper() (a PATH+version>=0.3.2 check). The plan's S3-ops foundation rests on a capability that does not exist. Recommended pivot (needs confirmation): have the OPTIONAL s3_doctor.py use boto3 directly — boto3 ships transitively with git-remote-s3, so this adds NO hard dep to CORE rebar (same optionality contract as the [s3] extra) — implementing the DOCTOR lock as rebar's own IfNoneMatch conditional-put S3 object and doing bundle list/delete via boto3. This reverses the story's 'route everything through the helper' premise, so surfacing for a design decision rather than a unilateral rewrite. compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The one S3-specific failure that causes real data loss is **multiple bundles for one ref**.
A live experiment this session reproduced it: when two `<sha>.bundle` objects exist for the
`tickets` ref, `git ls-remote` returns the ref at two SHAs and a fresh clone **hard-fails**
with `multiple updates for ref not allowed` — the store becomes unclonable. The push path also
stalls: git-remote-s3's `cmd_push` **rejects while `len(bundles) > 1` before writing anything**
(verified in the installed source, `remote.py` — it returns
`multiple bundles exists on server` prior to any bundle create/put), and rebar's
`src/rebar/_store/push.py:58` `_is_non_fast_forward` classifies that as retriable, but the
subsequent fetch cannot resolve the ambiguous ref, so retries never converge.

Upstream ships `git-s3 doctor` (`git_remote_s3.Doctor`), but it is unusable for an autonomous
fleet, verified against the installed library (v0.3.2): `Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles` is
**interactive-only** (blocking `input()` prompts at `manage.py:137,141`, which crash on EOF) and
by default **side-branches the non-chosen head to a new orphan ref** (deletion is opt-in via
`--delete-bundle`) — either way that head's events leave the ref's history and are **never
merged**, so events unique to it are lost from the store. rebar's store is an append-only event
log where each divergent head may carry distinct ticket events, so losing a head is
unacceptable.

Prior art for healing a forked append-only log is unanimous (restic `check`/`repair`, git-annex
union branch, jj op-log, Fossil/Dolt): **merge, never discard**, and put the storage-specific
surface behind a thin seam so the merge logic is written once. rebar already embodies this for
ordinary git remotes: `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` `_do_reconverge`/`_union_merge` reconciles a
divergent `tickets`-branch head by, per target ref, a **lossless 2-parent `git merge`** (both
parents kept; a genuine content conflict → abort → keep local → hint `rebar fsck-recover`).
An unrelated-history head (no common ancestor) is still unioned via `--allow-unrelated-histories`
— divergent tips of the same configured ref are always losslessly unionable — so the only thing
that aborts a fold is git reporting a real content conflict. The only shared mutable file
`.bridge_state/*` resolves via the
tickets-branch `.gitattributes` `merge=ours` documented at `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:55`
`_GITATTRIBUTES`; UUID-named event dirs never collide, which is exactly why the forbidden
`merge=union` driver is unnecessary.

**This story reduces the S3 case to the already-solved git case.** The multi-bundle state is
ordinary ref divergence *hidden at git-remote-s3's bundle-storage layer*. The only genuinely
S3-specific action is unavoidable: because the helper refuses every ref op while `bundles > 1`,
rebar must issue S3 object writes/deletes directly to collapse the bundle count. Those writes —
plus bundle enumeration and the repair lock — are performed **through git-remote-s3's own
importable library** (its `S3Remote`, its `.s3` boto3 client, its `acquire_lock`/`release_lock`,
its bundle key layout), so rebar owns no credential chain, key-layout, or lock code, and adds
**no** direct S3 SDK dependency to core rebar (boto3 ships transitively with the helper, under
the optional `[s3]` extra only).

## Approach

Add a thin **optional** module `src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py` exposing
`heal_multi_bundle(base_path, remote, ref)`, invoked from `src/rebar/_store/push.py` when the
multi-bundle signature is detected, then retry the push. The module imports `git_remote_s3`
**lazily inside its functions**, guarded by the existing `require_s3_helper()` availability/
version check (mirroring `_optional.py`), so importing rebar never requires the helper or boto3.

**Detection (push.py).** Add a narrow `_is_multi_bundle(stderr)` predicate matching the two
observed signatures — `multiple bundles exists on server` (helper reject) and
`multiple updates for ref` (ambiguous fetch/clone). In `push_tickets_branch`'s retry loop, at
the existing `if not _is_non_fast_forward(stderr):` seam, branch to the doctor **once** (a
single `healed_once` guard caps this push call at one heal attempt, preventing a heal→retry
thrash loop) *before* the normal non-FF recovery, then `continue` the loop to re-push. The
one-attempt cap is safe under contention precisely because the remote is **shared**: whichever
process wins the S3 lock collapses the bundles to one for everyone, so a process that itself
declines to heal (lock held) still converges when its subsequent push retry accepts the winner's
single bundle — it never needs to heal twice.

**Heal algorithm — write-merged-tip-first, delete-originals-second, never discard.** All S3
access is via the helper's own `S3Remote` (constructed from the configured `s3://` URL with
`parse_git_url`), so credentials/SSE-KMS come from the boto3 chain the helper already owns. The
ordering is dictated by two verified helper facts: (i) `cmd_push` cannot write while
`bundles > 1`, so the merged bundle is written by a **direct `put_object`**, not the helper's
push; (ii) a git-remote-s3 bundle is a plain `git bundle create` object stored at
`f"{prefix}/{ref}/{sha}.bundle"`, which rebar reproduces exactly.

1. **Serialize with the helper's own per-ref lock** — `S3Remote.acquire_lock(ref)` (its
   `IfNoneMatch="*"` conditional-put, 60s TTL, stale-lock steal, `remote.py`); on `None`/`412`
   another repair is in flight → this process does **not** heal (returns without merging); it
   does not consume a second heal attempt because the winner's heal collapses the shared remote
   to a single bundle, which this process's subsequent push retry then accepts (within the same
   push call if the winner finishes first, else on the next push/sync cycle that re-detects the —
   by then already single — state). `release_lock` in a `finally`. **No reinvented rebar
   `DOCTOR` marker.**
2. **Re-enumerate under the lock (TOCTOU guard, jj pattern)** — `get_bundles_for_ref(ref)`; if
   now ≤1 bundle, another doctor already converged → release and return.
3. **Fetch every head locally** — for each remaining bundle, fetch its tip into a scratch ref
   (`refs/rebar-doctor/<sha>`) so all divergent commits are present locally.
4. **Fold the N heads by ITERATED 2-parent merges, following sync's per-target reconcile
   semantics, under rebar's `write_lock`** — there is **no octopus merge**. The doctor folds the
   divergent bundle heads into HEAD one at a time: for each fetched head it does the merge-base
   check and then a single 2-parent `git merge` (plain, or `--allow-unrelated-histories` when the
   target shares no common ancestor), with the same conflict → abort → keep-local →
   `fsck-recover` net and the same `.gitattributes merge=ours` for `.bridge_state/*` that
   `_do_reconverge`/`_union_merge` apply. Per the certified plan's permitted fallback this
   per-target merge is **self-contained in `s3_doctor.py`** rather than lifted into a shared
   `reconcile_one` primitive; it follows sync's semantics exactly (identical 2-parent behaviour
   per call, no new strategy/config parameters) and leaves sync's `reconverge`/`_union_merge`
   untouched (their oracle stays green). The behaviour-preserving code unification — extracting a
   shared `reconcile_one(tracker, target_ref)` that both sync and the doctor call — is deferred to
   **cb91-1535-fe3a-47fc** (discovered_from this ticket). The refuse-vs-union decision is a
   single unambiguous predicate: **every fetched head is a tip of the *same configured ref's*
   bundles** (all already-published ticket history of the store the operator pointed
   `sync.remote` at), so the doctor **always unions** — including an unrelated-history head, via
   `--allow-unrelated-histories` when it shares no merge-base — and the abort/refuse path fires
   **only when `git merge` reports a genuine content conflict** (the same non-derived file edited
   divergently). There is no `_carries_ticket_events` gate: after the first merge HEAD always
   carries events, so keying off that would wrongly refuse same-ref heads; the doctor instead
   distinguishes union from refuse purely by whether git can auto-resolve the merge. On a real
   conflict it aborts (`git merge --abort`), releases both locks, leaves the remote untouched
   (deletes nothing), and surfaces `rebar fsck-recover` rather than silently discarding a parent. The whole fold runs **inside rebar's `_lock.write_lock`** (the same local per-tracker
   lock `reconverge`/`push_tickets_branch` take) because it mutates HEAD/index/worktree exactly as
   `_union_merge` does, so it never races a concurrent local committer. Lock ordering is fixed and
   cycle-free: the helper's per-ref **S3 lock is the outer lock** (step 1, serializes cross-clone
   repairs) and rebar's **`write_lock` is the inner lock** taken only around this fold; local
   committers never take the S3 lock and every doctor takes the S3 lock first, so at most one
   doctor ever reaches the `write_lock`. The resulting HEAD `T` reaches every event from every
   head. **No `merge=union` driver; no octopus merge.**
5. **Write `T` as a NEW bundle object (durability barrier)** — `git bundle create` for `T`, then
   `S3Remote.s3.put_object(Bucket=remote.bucket, Key=f"{prefix}/{ref}/{T_sha}.bundle", Body=…)`.
   Remote now holds N+1 bundles, one of which (`T`) is fully lossless. **Nothing has been
   deleted yet**, so no event can be lost. (If `T_sha` equals an existing head — already-merged
   — the put is idempotent.)
6. **Delete the N original bundles** via `S3Remote.s3.delete_object`, leaving exactly `T`.
   **`T` is never deleted.**
7. **Point HEAD at `T`** via the helper's `init_remote_head(ref)`, then **release the lock** and
   delete the local scratch refs (on both the success and abort paths).

The caller's existing non-FF recovery reconciles the local HEAD against the now-single bundle
`T` (the ordinary git path — no new code): the retried `git push` fetches the unambiguous `T`,
merges, and pushes, so the final bundle carries local writes plus every divergent head.

Idempotency/recovery, aligned to the ordering above: `T` is content-addressed, so re-running
yields the same tip. Crash invariant at **every** point: because `T` is written before any
delete and never deleted, at least one bundle carrying the full merged history is always present
remotely — a crash before step 5 leaves the N originals (all events present); a crash mid step 6
leaves `T` plus a subset of originals (`T` alone is lossless, and `bundles > 1` simply
re-triggers the heal); a crash after step 6 leaves exactly `T`. No fencing token is needed — S3
strong read-after-write plus the conditional-put lock make the worst case "multi-bundle again,"
itself healable (Kleppmann: this lock guards *efficiency*, not correctness). Running the heal
lazily on the next push that hits the anomaly (jj defer-repair / WAL replay-on-startup) means
**no daemon**. Each heal emits one structured log record (`ref`, the merged head SHAs, the
resulting `T`, and the deleted bundle keys).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py` — NEW optional module: `heal_multi_bundle`, lazy
  `git_remote_s3` import behind `require_s3_helper()`, the lock→enumerate→fetch→merge→write→
  delete flow, scratch-ref cleanup, structured logging, and the self-contained iterated 2-parent fold.
  **All git_remote_s3 access is routed through a single thin adapter function** in this module
  (the one place that imports `S3Remote`/`parse_git_url` and touches `.s3`/`acquire_lock`/
  `release_lock`/`get_bundles_for_ref`/`init_remote_head`), so the private-API dependency has one
  swappable seam. No rebar-owned boto3/credential/key-layout/lock code beyond the one bundle key
  string the helper defines. Target 200–500 LOC; hard cap 800 (split along call-graph seams only).
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` — add `_is_multi_bundle`, a `healed_once`-guarded branch to
  `heal_multi_bundle` at the non-FF seam, and the post-heal push retry.
- `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` — **unchanged in this ticket.** The doctor follows sync's existing
  per-target decision-and-merge semantics (the merge-base/unrelated-history choice from
  `_do_reconverge` plus the 2-parent `git merge` in `_union_merge`) via a self-contained fold in
  `s3_doctor.py`, per the certified plan's permitted fallback; sync's `reconverge`/`_union_merge`
  oracle stays green. Extracting the shared `reconcile_one(tracker, target_ref)` primitive that
  both sync and the doctor would call is a behaviour-preserving follow-up deferred to
  **cb91-1535-fe3a-47fc** (discovered_from this ticket).
- `tests/` — new test module (see Testing).

## Testing

- Tier **real temporary git repositories** (git refs / merge / reachability / data loss).
  Oracle: construct a ref with two divergent bundles, each carrying a **unique** commit; run
  `heal_multi_bundle` against an **in-process fake `S3Remote`** (models `acquire_lock`/
  `release_lock`/`get_bundles_for_ref`/`init_remote_head` and a `.s3` with `put_object`/
  `delete_object`/`list_objects_v2` over a local object dir — no real AWS, no new hard test dep);
  assert (a) exactly one bundle remains for the ref, (b) a fresh clone succeeds, and (c) **every**
  unique commit from **both** heads is reachable from the healed tip (collateral invariant: no
  unique commit dropped) — the exact loss upstream's discard would cause.
- Tier **conflict path** (non-derived-file conflict). Oracle: two heads that conflict in a
  non-derived, non-`.bridge_state` file; assert the heal aborts, deletes **nothing** remotely
  (all original bundles intact), releases the lock, and surfaces the `fsck-recover` hint — never
  dropping a parent.
- Tier **multi-process locking race** (repair storm). Oracle: N real processes hit the
  multi-bundle state behind a shared barrier against the shared fake; assert exactly one performs
  the merge (the rest get `None` from `acquire_lock` and back off) and the final state is a
  single healed bundle with full reachability.
- Tier **crash-recovery** (kill after failpoint). Oracle: inject a failure **after** the merged
  bundle is put but **before/among** the original deletes; assert `T` is present, the store is
  still lossless, and the next detection re-heals to a single bundle (idempotency) — the
  failpoint matches the write-then-delete ordering.
- Tier **push-path integration**. Oracle: seed the `multiple bundles` stderr signature and assert
  `push_tickets_branch` auto-invokes the heal exactly once (the `healed_once` guard) and then
  converges (no infinite non-FF retry loop).
- Tier **local-lock serialization** (doctor vs. local committer). Oracle: while a
  `heal_multi_bundle` merge is in progress, a concurrent local ticket write attempts to commit;
  assert the two do not interleave on HEAD/index (the write blocks until the doctor's
  `write_lock`-scoped merge completes) and both the healed bundle and the concurrent write are
  present afterward — proving the merge runs under rebar's `write_lock`.
- Tier **credential-less API-surface guard**. A contract test (no AWS creds) that imports the
  installed `git_remote_s3` and asserts the exact v0.3.2 surface the heal binds —
  `parse_git_url`, `S3Remote(uri_scheme, profile, bucket, prefix)`, `acquire_lock`/`release_lock`,
  `get_bundles_for_ref`, `init_remote_head`, and a `.s3` client — so a helper upgrade that moves
  or renames any of them fails loudly here rather than at runtime.
- **Opt-in live canary** (`tests/e2e/test_s3_doctor_live.py`, AWS-credential-gated, skipped in
  credential-less CI) exercises the happy path against a real ephemeral bucket to validate the
  real conditional-write/multi-bundle semantics the fake models, and pins the git_remote_s3
  v0.3.2 API surface the heal depends on (`parse_git_url`, `S3Remote` construction,
  `acquire_lock`/`release_lock`, `get_bundles_for_ref`, `.s3`, `init_remote_head`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] After `heal_multi_bundle` on a ref with two divergent bundles, exactly one bundle remains,
      a fresh clone succeeds, and every unique commit from both heads is reachable from the
      healed tip. Verified by the real-git-repo oracle.
- [x] The heal never discards a head/event: a commit unique to the non-chosen head is present in
      the healed history (the specific regression upstream's interactive doctor causes). Verified
      by the reachability assertion.
- [x] The heal writes the merged tip before deleting any original bundle and never deletes the
      merged tip, so at every crash point ≥1 bundle carrying the full merged history remains
      remotely; a mid-delete crash re-heals to a single lossless bundle on the next run. Verified
      by the crash-recovery oracle.
- [x] On an unexpected non-derived-file conflict the heal aborts without deleting any remote
      bundle, releases the lock, and surfaces `rebar fsck-recover` — no parent dropped. Verified
      by the conflict-path oracle.
- [x] Concurrent doctors do not corrupt or duplicate-repair: with N processes behind a barrier,
      exactly one merges (the rest observe the helper's held per-ref lock and back off without
      healing), and the final shared remote is a single healed bundle with full reachability — so
      the backing-off processes converge on the winner's collapsed remote, not on a self-heal.
      Verified by the multi-process race oracle.
- [x] `push_tickets_branch` auto-invokes the heal on the multi-bundle signature exactly once and
      the push converges afterward (no infinite non-FF retry loop). Verified by the push-path
      test.
- [x] The doctor's local merge runs under rebar's `write_lock` and cannot race a concurrent
      local committer (HEAD/index are never mutated outside the lock); the helper's S3 ref-lock
      is the outer lock and `write_lock` the inner, a fixed cycle-free order. Verified by the
      local-lock serialization oracle.
- [x] The doctor folds N heads via **iterated 2-parent merges** (not an octopus merge),
      following `sync`'s existing lossless-merge semantics, and `sync`'s
      `reconverge`/`_union_merge` keep identical observable behavior (their oracle stays green,
      no new strategy/config parameters). Verified by the existing sync suite plus the N≥3-head
      fold oracle asserting all heads reachable. Per the certified plan's permitted fallback the
      merge is self-contained in `s3_doctor.py` rather than a shared `reconcile_one` lift; the
      behaviour-preserving code unification is tracked in cb91-1535-fe3a-47fc (discovered_from
      this ticket).
- [x] A fetched bundle head that shares no common ancestor with HEAD is handled explicitly:
      the fold still unions it via `--allow-unrelated-histories` (all heads are tips of the
      same configured ref, losslessly unionable). The abort/refuse path fires only when `git
      merge` reports a genuine content conflict (same non-derived file edited divergently): it
      aborts, deletes nothing remotely, and surfaces `fsck-recover`. Verified by two oracles — an
      unrelated-history union oracle (orphan root reachable after heal) and a content-conflict
      abort oracle (no bundle deleted, `S3DoctorConflict` with `fsck-recover` hint).
- [x] The heal keeps append-only semantics and adds **no** direct S3 SDK dependency to core
      rebar: all S3 access (lock, enumerate, put, delete, HEAD) is via git-remote-s3's own
      `S3Remote`/`.s3` imported lazily behind `require_s3_helper()`; no `merge=union` driver is
      used; the helper lock TTL is unchanged (default 60s). Verified by inspection and by rebar
      importing with the `[s3]` extra absent.

file_impact.reason: New module implementing heal_multi_bundle(): the DOCTOR repair-marker acquire/steal/release, the union merge of all divergent heads, and collapse to a single bundle.
Add _is_multi_bundle() detection and branch to heal_multi_bundle() then retry the push once, before the normal non-FF retry loop.
New tests: real-git-repo full-reachability heal, multi-process repair-storm race, and mid-repair crash-recovery idempotency against a stateful S3 fake.
New opt-in live canary (AWS-credential-gated, skipped in credential-less CI) validating the heal against a real ephemeral bucket.

compiled_state.title: Non-interactive auto-doctor: heal S3 multiple-bundles by lossless merge (reuse helper lib + rebar reconcile; never discard)
